title: ESP-NOW: direct ESP32 communication without a router

spans.text:
ESP-NOW is Espressif's Wi-Fi-based protocol for short messages between nearby ESP devices without joining an IP network. It is useful for sensor reports, remotes, smart lights, and small multi-node systems; it does not need a router or internet. It is not ordinary Wi-Fi networking or an internet connection. Both devices must support ESP-NOW, use the same Wi-Fi channel, and know the receiver's MAC address.

The sender starts Wi-Fi in station mode, initializes ESP-NOW, adds a peer, and sends a message. A successful return from

means the packet was accepted for transmission, not that the receiver application processed it. For reliable delivery, design an application acknowledgement, retry, sequence number, and timeout. A receiver separately registers a receive callback; its signature can vary with the Arduino-ESP32 version.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Encryption is disabled in this teaching sketch and the MAC address is an example. For a real device, verify the peer address, configure encryption with appropriate PMK/LMK keys, validate incoming data, and do not broadcast secrets. Packet limits, callback APIs, and coexistence with Wi-Fi depend on chip and core version; check the ESP-IDF documentation for the exact target.
